content.title: About
content.content: Borscht is a traditional Eastern European soup made with beetroot, meat, cabbage and other vegetables. It has a vivid red color, a rich flavor, and is often served with sour cream and fresh herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Borscht originated in Ukraine and is considered a national dish.
Traditional recipes use a meat broth, but vegetarian versions are common.
Beetroot gives the soup its characteristic red hue and is high in beta‑carotene.
Regional variations exist: Russian borscht often includes beans, Polish versions may add mushrooms.
Borscht can be served cold in summer and hot in winter.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Beetroot contains betalains, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cabbage and carrots provide dietary fiber that promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Source of vitamins
items.content: Borscht supplies vitamin C, vitamin B6 and folate, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When prepared with moderate meat, borscht remains a low‑fat dish.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high liquid content helps maintain the body’s water balance.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Traditional recipes often use a lot of salt, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to beef, pork, or certain vegetables.

items.title: Nitrate content
items.content: Beetroot can contain nitrates; excessive intake may lead to nitrite formation.

items.title: Calorie increase with sour cream
items.content: Adding sour cream raises calories and saturated fat levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve borscht hot, typically topped with a dollop of sour cream, fresh dill or parsley, and a slice of rye bread. Optional additions include boiled eggs or beans for extra protein.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the soup to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it keeps for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
